problem: Consider the section of the parabola $3{x}^{2}+4y=1$ that lies in the fourth quadrant.  Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$  and that $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=-\frac{1}{4}$ on the parabola at the point where $y=-\frac{1}{2},$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.

feedback.problem: Consider the section of the hyperbola $\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-{y}^{2}=1$ that lies in the first quadrant. Given that $x=x(t),$ $y=y(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=6$ on the curve at the point where $x=2\sqrt{3},$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point.
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-{y}^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3})-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({y}^{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}({y}^{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (\frac{2x}{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2y) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=6$ and $x=2\sqrt{3}.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot (\frac{2\cdot 2\sqrt{3}}{3})-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot (2y) & =0 \\ 8\sqrt{3}-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2y & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We also want to substitute for $y,$ but we are not given this value. However, we can find it by substituting $x=2\sqrt{3}$ into the equation of the hyperbola.   

At the point where $x=2\sqrt{3},$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-{y}^{2} & =1 \\ \frac{(2\sqrt{3})^{2}}{3}-{y}^{2} & =1 \\ 4-{y}^{2} & =1 \\ {y}^{2} & =3 \\ y & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used $y>0$ since we're only interested in the first quadrant. 

Finally, substituting $y=\sqrt{3},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}8\sqrt{3}-\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2(\sqrt{3}) & =0 \\ 8\sqrt{3}-2\sqrt{3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
